items.title: Many Steps into One: Reasoning Contraction and the Limits of Safe Memory Reuse for LLM Agents
items.abstract: Thought templates, skill libraries, agent memories and caches turn many reasoning steps into one. We call this reasoning contraction. A contracted memory saves reasoning steps and errors until its facts change, then quietly answers wrong. Most systems trust memories by counting successes and failures. We prove that such counters are badly tuned change detectors: a symmetric counter notices a partial change only after a power of its false-alarm horizon, and an unclipped one may never notice it. On five LLMs answering multi-hop questions over edited facts, ExpeL- and ACE-style counters serve 7.0-13.5x more stale answers than certified memories given the same information, and on code tasks with an exact verifier 35-73x more. Safety also has a price. When facts change and each memory is judged only by its own verified outcomes, one number, the certification load, sets how much reasoning any safe memory can skip, and under Zipf demand it yields a scaling law. Our recipe weighs each memory's failures by its own likelihood ratio, certifies its utility against live reasoning, and restarts the certificate when facts change, with the likelihood-ratio detector as the safety net for unannounced changes; for large edits it also invalidates the memory.

items.title: Mechanisms of Brand Authenticity Erosion in AI-Generated Advertising: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in advertising since 2022 has transformed content production while raising concerns about the preservation of brand authenticity, a critical foundation of consumer trust and brand relationships. This study examines how AI-generated advertising influences perceived brand authenticity, identifies the mechanisms driving authenticity erosion, and explains the contextual factors that account for inconsistent findings in prior research. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, this review synthesizes 13 studies published between 2022 and 2026 retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and EBSCOhost databases. Through thematic synthesis, this study identifies three interrelated mechanisms through which AI-generated advertising may undermine brand authenticity: disclosure effects, failed anthropomorphism, and sincerity erosion. The findings further reveal that the effects of AI-generated advertising on authenticity perceptions are contingent upon individual characteristics, product and brand contexts, and source-related factors, including AI capability beliefs, product type, luxury positioning, and communicator characteristics. This study develops an integrated framework explaining when and why AI-generated advertising enhances or undermines brand authenticity, thus providing theoretical insights for consumer research and practical implications for AI-enabled marketing decision-making.

items.title: Mechanization and Agronomic Approaches for Reducing Farm Drudgery and Labour Requirement in Agriculture: A Critical Narrative Review
items.abstract: Agricultural work remains physically demanding and strongly seasonal in many production systems, while labour scarcity, rising wages, ageing farm populations, and competing non-farm employment are increasing pressure to complete operations with less human effort. This critical narrative review evaluates how mechanization and agronomic redesign can reduce farm drudgery and labour requirement without assuming that labour saved at an individual task is equivalent to labour displaced from agriculture. Literature published from 1 January 1990 to 6 August 2026 was identified through accessible scholarly databases and indexes, supplemented by citation searching and authoritative institutional sources. Evidence was appraised for study design, measurement of labour and ergonomic outcomes, external validity, treatment of confounding, duration, and attention to gender, safety, and implementation conditions. The strongest evidence indicates that mechanization can markedly reduce time and physiological burden in power-intensive and repetitive operations, but whole-farm labour effects vary because mechanization also changes cultivated area, input intensity, timeliness, and the allocation of family and hired labour. Ergonomic hand tools and scale-appropriate machines are especially important where capital-intensive mechanization is infeasible. Agronomic approaches such as zero or reduced tillage and direct-seeded rice can remove labour-intensive operations, yet their labour-saving value is conditional on weed control, crop establishment, residue management, and access to compatible equipment. Conservation agriculture illustrates this conditionality: manual planting basins or increased hand weeding can offset labour savings, whereas mechanized establishment and effective weed management can reduce peak labour demand. Gendered task allocation, machinery access, custom hiring services, occupational safety, and rural employment transitions determine who benefits and who bears adjustment costs. Robotics and autonomous equipment may address labour shortages in selected systems, but economic feasibility, field reliability, supervision, and human-machine safety remain important constraints. The review concludes that drudgery reduction is best pursued through integrated mechanization-agronomy packages evaluated with task-specific ergonomic measures and whole-household, whole-season labour accounting.

items.title: Media neophraseologisms as a marker of transformational and innovative processes in the Russian phraseological system
items.abstract: This article is devoted to a comprehensive study of media neophraseologisms as relevant markers of transformation processes in the modern Russian phraseological system. Using extensive empirical data from the Russian-language online press and Telegram channels for 2020–2026, the article identifies key derivational trends in neophraseology: structural diffuseness, pragmemization, and sententialization of signs. We demonstrate a semantic shift in neoidioms toward de-abstraction and connection to the current agenda and substantiate the adaptive nature of phraseological innovations in the context of an increasingly complex information picture of the world. Particular attention is paid to the anthropocentric aspect of linguistic creativity: The generation of neophraseologisms, mediated by the mechanisms of irony, allusion, and manipulation, is verified as a demarcation line between the natural human text generation and the algorithms of generative artificial intelligence. We propose a typology of neophraseologisms, including discursive-precedent, intermedia, and calqued units, including their axiological and ludic functions in media texts. The article notes that the diffuseness of structure and pragmemization act as mechanisms of linguistic economy, while the de-abstraction of signs reflects the connection between phraseology and extralinguistic factors. The results are significant for lexicographic practice, university teaching, and media stylistics. The developed typology and the identified derivational processes can serve as a basis for monitoring the Russian phraseological system evolution. The results of the study are applicable in lexicographic practice, teaching, and media stylistics.

items.title: MEDICAL REHABILITATION OF MUSCULOSKELETAL DISORDER
items.abstract: Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) are conditions affecting the muscles, bones, joints, tendons, ligaments, cartilage, and other supporting structures of the body. They may be acute or chronic and can result from trauma, repetitive movements, poor posture, aging, genetic factors, occupational hazards, or inflammatory diseases. Common musculoskeletal disorders include osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoporosis, low back pain, tendinitis, bursitis, fractures, and muscle strains.The main symptoms are pain, swelling, stiffness, muscle weakness, restricted joint movements, and difficulty performing daily activities. Diagnosis is based on medical history, physical examination, and investigations such as X-rays, CT scans, MRI, blood tests, and bone mineral density measurements, depending on the condition.Treatment aims to relieve pain, reduce inflammation, restore mobility, and prevent disability. Management includes medications, physiotherapy, therapeutic exercises, heat and cold therapy, occupational therapy, and lifestyle modifications. In severe cases, surgical intervention may be necessary. Medical rehabilitation plays an essential role in improving muscle strength, joint flexibility, balance, coordination, and functional independence.Prevention involves maintaining correct posture, regular physical activity, a balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D, maintaining a healthy body weight, using proper workplace ergonomics, and avoiding repetitive strain. Early diagnosis and appropriate treatment help reduce complications and improve quality of life. A multidisciplinary approach involving doctors, physiotherapists, and occupational therapists is essential for effective management and long-term recovery.

items.abstract: Digital technology has evolved rapidly, resulting in a new form of marketing known as "meta marketing," which represents a revolutionary way of doing business in today's rapidly changing marketplace, especially for marketers working within the highly competitive Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG) industry.This study aimed to conceptually explore how organizations utilize technology such as the Metaverse, augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), and artificial intelligence (AI) to create meta marketing strategies, while promoting sustainable development.This will include investigating how using immersive, interactive marketing environments can motivate consumer engagement, trust, and purchasing behaviours, while at the same time, through lessening physical consumption of resources and improving digital communications, developing initiatives that encompass environmental sustainability.Using existing literature and applying theoretical frameworks, this research advances knowledge by developing a conceptual framework that connects the advancement of technological innovation with achieving sustainable outcomes as a business performance indicator.Overall, this study provides evidence that the use of Meta marketing presents FMCG companies with an opportunity to gain a competitive advantage while meeting sustainability challenges.

items.title: Metaheuristic Approaches for the Satisfiability Problem (SAT): A Systematic Review and Comparative Study with Modern SAT Solvers
items.abstract: The Boolean Satisfiability Problem is a central challenge in artificial intelligence and combinatorial optimization, with applications in circuit verification, planning, and bioinformatics. This study makes two main contributions: a systematic review of metaheuristic approaches conducted under the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) protocol, and a comparative evaluation of 11 algorithms. The considered methods include genetic algorithms, genetic algorithms with stepwise adaptation of weights, hybrid grey wolf genetic algorithms, genetic-based local search, population-based simulated annealing, dynamic clause weighting local search, stochastic local search, phase transition-based local search, random walk with local (1 + 1) evolutionary algorithm, improved adaptive genetic algorithm, and artificial bee colony. The evaluation relies on multiple criteria, including solution quality, robustness, success rate with confidence intervals, computational efficiency, and scalability across the benchmark families UF20 to UF250, complemented by additional benchmarks from the SAT Challenge Random Track (2018) and newly generated random 3-SAT instances. The results show that Genetic Algorithm, phase transition-based local search, dynamic clause weighting local search, genetic-based local search, random walk with local (1+1) Evolutionary Algorithm, and Artificial Bee Colony provide the most robust performance, maintaining a balance between exploration and exploitation. Beyond comparisons within metaheuristics, the study also examines how bio-inspired approaches compare with modern SAT solvers based on conflict-driven clause learning and stochastic local search across different problem scales. By contrast, highly specialized variants, such as genetic algorithms with stepwise adaptation of weights, population-based simulated annealing, hybrid grey wolf genetic algorithms, and improved adaptive genetic algorithms, degrade significantly on larger benchmarks. Overall, this study consolidates the strengths and weaknesses of metaheuristics and outlines future directions for adaptability, hybridization with machine learning, and scalable computations.

items.abstract: The article analyzes the penetration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools into programming education, their didactic opportunities and risks. A four-component methodological model is proposed for using AI tools while preserving students' independent programming skills and algorithmic thinking: staged use of AI, developing AI-collaboration competence, renewing the assessment system, and project-based learning. The model can be applied in teaching programming and computer science at higher education institutions.

items.title: Methodologies for AI-Driven Renewable Energy Optimization
items.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies and computer networks has triggered the sudden leap in the world energy requirements and heightened the stress on the idea of environmental sustainability. The renewable energy sources, such as solar, wind and hydro sources, are very attractive alternatives to fossil fuels but due to their intermittency nature, there are serious issues related to the forecasting accuracy, energy storage and grid stability. The chapter is a survey of various methodological strategies in optimizing renewable energy systems that are based on data-centric, AI-based tools that include machine-learning models, digital-twin systems, metaheuristic optimization algorithms, and lifecycle assessment models. These methods of computation increase the level of energy forecasting, simplify the real-time monitoring of the working system, optimize energy distribution, and manage storage resources.

items.title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
items.abstract: Multi-objective molecular optimization is a critical process in drug discovery that aims to modify a given molecule to simultaneously improve multiple properties while maintaining a similar overall structure. This process often requires iterative modifications guided by computational or experimental feedback. Recent large language model (LLM)-based methods have begun to explore this iterative approach; however, these methods are not explicitly trained to leverage such feedback, while existing approaches primarily focus on single-turn molecular optimization. To address this gap, we introduce Multi-turn Feedback Guided (MFG) molecular optimization, a reinforcement learning framework that trains an LLM to progressively optimize molecules using feedback from previous turns. MFG introduces a feedback vector capturing both property improvements and source molecule similarity, alongside a feedback-aligned reward function that promotes progressive improvement across turns. We apply MFG over $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$, a state-of-the-art LLM model for multi-objective molecular optimization, evaluate $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ on ten multi-objective molecular optimization tasks. The results demonstrate that $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ achieves the highest average similarity-constrained success rate ($81.50%$), outperforming the base model $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$ ($70.81%$).

items.title: Microfluidics in Biomedical Applications: Fundamental Principles, Fabrication Technologies, Emerging Diagnostic Platforms, Organ-on-Chip Systems, Drug Development and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Microfluidics has emerged as an important platform for manipulating and analyzing small volumes of fluids, cells, biomolecules, and particles with high precision. Its ability to control microscale flows and integrate multiple analytical steps has enabled diverse biomedical technologies, including lab-on-a-chip, point-of-care diagnostics, organ-on-chip, and microphysiological systems. This review summarizes the fundamental principles of biomedical microfluidics, including microscale fluid dynamics, laminar flow, diffusion, and key dimensionless parameters, together with major platform formats such as continuous-flow, droplet-based, and digital microfluidics. Recent fabrication approaches, including photolithography, soft lithography, molding, laser-based methods, 3D printing, micromilling, and paper- and lamination-based techniques, are also discussed. The review highlights applications in cancer and liquid biopsy, infectious disease diagnostics, cardiovascular and neurological disorders, organ-on-chip models, drug screening and toxicity testing, pharmaceutical synthesis, drug delivery, single-cell analysis, and regenerative and reproductive medicine. Particular attention is given to the growing use of microfluidics for personalized and human-relevant biomedical research. The review further examines the major challenges associated with microfluidic biomedical systems, including fabrication reproducibility, material compatibility, biological complexity, standardization, scalability and manufacturing, clinical validation, regulatory requirements, and integration with advanced computational approaches such as artificial intelligence and machine learning. Finally, future perspectives are discussed, with particular emphasis on personalized medicine, decentralized diagnostics, human-relevant drug development, multi-organ microphysiological systems, wearable and implantable microfluidics, and automated biomedical platforms.

items.title: MiND: Minimal Deterministic Middleware for Auditable Large Language Model Interactions
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded in research software, yet many integrations preserve only the visible prompt and answer while losing structured evidence about configuration, provider metadata, timing, failures, and the exact request procedure. MiND is an open-source, provider-neutral middleware that places a small audit boundary between an application and an LLM. For each attempted interaction it normalizes the input, constructs an explicit request, invokes a provider adapter, normalizes the result, and stores a versioned Cycle Artifact containing the observable execution context. The same core is available through a Python API, command-line interface, local HTTP API, and a self-contained Windows interface. MiND is deliberately non-agentic: it does not infer human intention, expose hidden model reasoning, or claim deterministic repetition of stochastic model output. Its purpose is narrower—to make the surrounding execution procedure inspectable and reusable.

items.title: Mitigating Domain Shift and Dataset Bias in Deep Learning Models for Cancer Diagnostics
items.abstract: Abstract The translation of deep learning architectures from controlled experimental settings into real-world cancer diagnostics is heavily bottlenecked by domain shift and demographic bias. While models routinely achieve near-perfect retrospective performance on internal datasets, validation across external multicenter cohorts incurs a systemic and severe performance degradation, with an average metric drop of 0.16 AUC. This review provides a comprehensive metasynthesis of contemporary algorithmic mitigation paradigms designed to alleviate distribution discrepancies, evaluating techniques ranging from classical stain normalization and adversarial feature alignment to test-time adaptation and large-scale self-supervised pathology foundation models. Our analysis reveals a critical dichotomy between raw diagnostic performance and algorithmic equity: current optimization frameworks that successfully elevate aggregate macro metrics frequently do so by obscuring or actively exacerbating underlying demographic and subpopulation disparities. To achieve safe, equitable, and universally reliable clinical artificial intelligence, the field must transcend static validation habits. We outline a future roadmap anchored on three critical axes: establishing intersectional disparity indices as primary regulatory endpoints, standardizing multivendor metadata-rich benchmarks, and prioritizing.

items.title: MMTA: Benchmarking Multimodal Temporal Analysis with Time Series, Text, and Vision
items.abstract: Time-series analysis is increasingly studied in multimodal settings, yet most benchmarks pair temporal signals with text or with visualizations derived from the same signal. This leaves open whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can integrate time series with real-world visual evidence. We introduce MMTA (multimodal temporal analysis), a benchmark of tri-modal tasks with diverse cross-modal complementarity patterns among time series, text, and vision. MMTA spans nine domains -- robotics, autonomous driving, human action, manufacturing, AR assistance, healthcare, recommendation, finance, and climate -- under video+TS and image+TS layouts, with a 3,524-sample test split covering classification and forecasting. The benchmark standardizes heterogeneous real-world sources into a shared schema with domain-specific prompts, provenance documentation, and success-weighted metrics that penalize both wrong answers and failed generations. Evaluating eight open-source and proprietary MLLMs reveals a shared bottleneck: representing time series as text creates very long token sequences and weakens fine-grained alignment with visual evidence, especially in long-video settings. items.title: Mobilising AI Capability for Sustainable Supply‐Chain Transformation: The Mediating Role of Green Lean Six Sigma
items.abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) capability can be mobilised as a strategic organisational capability for sustainable supply‐chain transformation. Integrating the Natural Resource‐Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory and Sociotechnical Systems Theory, the study argues that AI‐enabled sensing and decision support do not automatically translate into sustainability outcomes; strategic value emerges when technological resources, managerial competencies, human expertise and process routines are aligned. Green Lean Six Sigma (GLSS) is therefore conceptualised as an organisational architecture that converts AI‐generated insight into disciplined problem definition, waste and variation reduction, process redesign, standardisation and continuous improvement. Survey data from 361 managers and executives in supply‐chain‐intensive organisations across multiple Southeast Asian countries and sectors were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling. AI capability is positively associated with GLSS implementation, whereas GLSS is positively associated with environmental, economic and social supply‐chain performance. Significant indirect effects further show that GLSS acts as the transmission mechanism linking AI capability to all three triple‐bottom‐line outcomes. Because the estimated structural model did not include direct AI capability‐to‐performance paths, the evidence is interpreted as support for indirect effects rather than as proof of partial mediation. The study contributes to business strategy and sustainability research by explaining how an AI capability becomes strategically valuable when embedded in a sociotechnical improvement architecture. It also offers a staged managerial road map for harmonising AI investment, GLSS techniques and sustainable business transformation.

items.title: Modelling Risk Factors of Urban Gas Accidents for Enhanced Energy Security: An Association Rule Mining Approach Integrating Causality Theory, 24‐Model, and HFACS
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Urban gas systems are core components of global energy infrastructure, underpinning residential, commercial, and industrial energy supply while supporting low‐carbon goals. However, the growing frequency of urban gas accidents—from pipeline leaks to explosions—poses severe threats to energy security, public safety, and sustainable urban development, largely due to insufficient systematic analysis of root causes. This study addresses this gap by integrating accident causality theory, the 24‐Model, and the Human Factor Analysis and Classification System (HFACS) to investigate 100 urban gas accidents, combining Chinese (2014–2023) and global datasets. Using Apriori‐based Association Rule Mining (ARM), we identified 9 key risk factors, 19 critical association rules, and a universal causal chain, with institutional negligence (inadequate regulatory frameworks and weak supervision) confirmed as the predominant root cause. The key causal chain is: “lack of targeted energy safety regulations → poor supervision of gas infrastructure → unaddressed safety hazards → equipment failure in delivery systems → gas leakage (and subsequent ignition) → accident occurrence.” To mitigate these risks, we propose three actionable strategies: tailored safety regulations for urban gas networks, AI‐enhanced real‐time supervision systems, and competency‐based training programs. These insights not only optimize the resilience of China's gas energy systems but also provide a transferable framework for global urban energy safety management, aligning with goals for secure and sustainable urban energy.

items.title: MONITORING STUDENTS' LEARNING OUTCOMES AND ASSESSING INDIVIDUAL DEVELOPMENT WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN A DIGITAL EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT
items.abstract: This paper provides a scientific and methodological analysis of monitoring students' learning outcomes and assessing their individual development with artificial intelligence (AI) in a digital educational environment. It examines the content of learning outcome monitoring, the components on which it relies (data sources, indicators, analytical methods and feedback), and the opportunities offered by AI-based learning analytics. It also defines three groups of criteria for assessing individual development: the dynamics of results, the achievement of learning goals, and independent work and reflection. As a result, a six-stage methodology is proposed in which the teacher keeps the final pedagogical decision. The methodology is intended to support the timely and individualised assessment of students in higher education institutions.

items.title: Motivation matters in the anesthesia workforce: intrinsic and extrinsic work motivation and burnout among anesthesia staff in Karbala, Iraq
items.abstract: Healthcare professionals in anesthesia and perioperative care face sustained occupational stress, yet little is known about how motivational orientation is associated with burnout vulnerability, particularly in conflict-affected, low-resource health systems. This study examined intrinsic and extrinsic work motivation in relation to personal, work-related, and client-related burnout among anesthesia staff in Karbala, Iraq, and tested whether motivational orientation explained variance beyond demographic and occupational characteristics. A cross-sectional design was employed. A convenience sample of 150 anesthesia staff was recruited from five public and teaching hospitals in Karbala, Iraq (September–December 2025). Participants completed Arabic versions of the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI) and Work Preference Inventory (WPI), alongside a demographic-occupational questionnaire. Hierarchical multiple regression analyses tested whether intrinsic and extrinsic motivation each explained incremental variance in burnout beyond covariates, and a combined model estimated their mutual (unique) contributions. Intrinsic motivation (M = 3.82, SD = 0.62) was negatively correlated with personal (ρ = −0.48), work-related (ρ = −0.19), and client-related burnout (ρ = −0.63). Extrinsic motivation (M = 3.23, SD = 0.61) was negatively correlated with personal (ρ = −0.31) and client-related burnout (ρ = −0.56) but not with work-related burnout (ρ = −0.11, p > 0.05); the two motivation scales were strongly intercorrelated (ρ = 0.84). After accounting for covariates, intrinsic motivation explained significant additional variance in personal (ΔR² = 0.209), work-related (ΔR² = 0.053), and client-related burnout (ΔR² = 0.416; all p < 0.01). Extrinsic motivation contributed significant incremental variance to personal and client-related burnout, though less strongly, and was not a significant predictor of work-related burnout ( p = 0.146). Demographic and occupational covariates accounted for minimal variance across all models. When both scales were entered together, intrinsic motivation remained a significant negative predictor of all three burnout dimensions, whereas extrinsic motivation became a significant positive predictor of personal and work-related burnout and was unrelated to client-related burnout (Table 3). In separate models, both intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, particularly intrinsic, were associated with lower burnout among anesthesia staff in a resource-constrained, conflict-affected setting (Karbala, Iraq). After mutual adjustment, only intrinsic motivation was consistently associated with lower burnout, whereas extrinsic motivation showed a positive association with personal and work-related burnout. Although the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, these findings describe associations only, and longitudinal or interventional research is needed to determine whether strengthening motivation could contribute to staff well-being strategies in similarly high-pressure environments. items.title: Multi-level point cloud transform regression via overlapping region prediction
items.abstract: Accurate and efficient point cloud registration is an important application of artificial intelligence for precise navigation and reliable decision-making in autonomous driving. However, the down-sampling of point clouds introduces interference from non-overlapping regions, resulting in the loss of important geometric information and a reduction in registration accuracy. Therefore, this study proposes an overlap-aware multi-level transformation regression network (OMTRNet), a deep-learning model that couples overlap prediction with frequency-domain and spatial feature interaction. Through a hierarchical feature extraction module designed with pixel grid mapping, we leverage the structural characteristics of pixel grids to efficiently extract point cloud features across multiple scales. By using a convolutional neural network-based overlap region prediction module, the overlap between the source and target point clouds at different scales is predicted. The overlapping region of the point cloud features is extracted from the predicted overlap, allowing for further feature extraction. Additionally, a frequency-domain feature interaction module is introduced to combine low-frequency global structural information with high-frequency local details as complementary cues for transformation estimation. Experimental results on the KITTI and NuScenes datasets validate the effectiveness of OMTRNet for large-scale partially overlapping point cloud registration. On the KITTI dataset, OMTRNet achieves an RTE of 0.2675 m, an RRE of 0.5342 deg, and a registration recall of 92.10%. The ablation results show that the DCT-based frequency-spatial interaction achieves competitive registration performance among the compared feature-interaction strategies.

items.title: Multimodal Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models in Embodied AI and Robotic Manipulation: Architectures, Cross-Embodiment Generalization, and Closed-Loop Latency Bounds
items.abstract: Abstract—Embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) and autonomous robotic manipulation are undergoing an architectural paradigm shift from narrow, task-specific behavioral cloning policies toward generalist Multimodal Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models. Pre-trained on Internet-scale vision-language corpora and fine-tuned across multi-robot demonstration datasets (e.g., Open X-Embodiment), VLA models—exemplified by RT-2, Octo, and OpenVLA—perceive high-resolution RGB-D sensor streams, process unstructured natural language instructions, and autoregressively predict or diffuse continuous 7-DoF robotic end-effector trajectories. However, translating disembodied multimodal foundation models into physical cyber-physical control fabrics introduces profound physical and computational bottlenecks: continuous action space tokenization discretization errors, severe cross-embodiment kinematic domain shifts across diverse robotic morphologies, closed-loop dynamic instability induced by non-deterministic neural inference latencies (>100 ms), and safety-critical execution failure modes. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of VLA models for robotic manipulation. We formalize the Markov Decision Process (MDP) bridging autoregressive tokenization with continuous trajectory diffusion policies, model cross-embodiment action normalization across disparate robotic arm kinematics, and derive Lyapunov-Krasovskii stability bounds under stochastic computational transport delays. Furthermore, we construct an empirical robotic evaluation testbed across physical Franka Emika Panda and simulated robotic workcells evaluating 600 complex manipulation trials spanning multi-stage semantic reasoning, spatial tool use, and long-horizon pick-and-place tasks. Our empirical findings demonstrate that continuous diffusion-policy action chunking achieves an 84.6% task success rate, outperforming discrete tokenization by 28.2% while reducing kinematic jerk by 62.4%. Concurrently, asynchronous visual-action decoupling bounds closed-loop inference latency within a deterministic 20 Hz control cycle. Finally, we formulate open research directions in tactile-integrated multi-modal perception, formal barrier certificates for physical safety, and self-supervised real-world policy refinement. Index Terms—Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models, Embodied AI, Robotic Manipulation, Diffusion Policy, Action Tokenization, Cross-Embodiment Generalization, Open X-Embodiment, Closed-Loop Control Latency.

items.abstract: Ikisiri Utafiti huu ulilenga kuchunguza mchango wa emoji katika ujenzi na ufasiri wa maana za kipragmatiki katika diskosi za kidijitali za Kiswahili. Ingawa matumizi ya emoji yameongezeka katika mawasiliano ya mitandao ya kijamii, bado haijaelezwa kwa makini namna emoji zinavyoashiria msimamo wa mwasilishaji, kuimarisha kauli, kupunguza au kuongeza utata na kutekeleza matendo ya usemi kwa kuzingatia muktadha na dhamira ya mtumaji. Utafiti uliongozwa na Nadharia ya Umuhimu ya Sperber na Wilson (1995) na kutumia muundo wa kimaelezo. Data kuu zilijumuisha emoji 285 za aina 11 zilizokusanywa kimakusudi kutoka katika diskosi za Kiswahili kwenye WhatsApp na X. Aidha, washiriki 50 waliteuliwa kimakusudi ili kufasiri na kuthibitisha maana za emoji kulingana na muktadha. Data za ziada zilikusanywa kwa kutumia dodoso, mahojiano na majadiliano ya makundi lengwa. Emoji 285 zilitumika katika uchanganuzi mkuu, huku maoni ya washiriki yakisaidia ufasiri wake. Data zilichanganuliwa na kuwasilishwa kwa njia ya maelezo. Matokeo yalionyesha kuwa maana za emoji hujengwa kupitia mwingiliano wa vipengele vya kiisimu, kiutamaduni, kisemiotiki, kiteknolojia na kimwingiliano. Emoji zilibainika kuashiria mtazamo na dhamira ya mwasilishaji, kuimarisha au kurekebisha nguvu ya kauli, kutekeleza matendo ya usemi na kuelekeza ufasiri kulingana na muktadha. Utafiti huu unachangia uelewa wa emoji kama rasilimali za kipragmatiki na kutoa msingi wa tafiti zijazo kuhusu uchakataji wa lugha asilia kwa kutumia akili unde na maendeleo ya lugha za Kiafrika katika teknolojia ya kisasa. AbstractThis study examined the contribution of emojis to the construction and interpretation of pragmatic meaning in digital Kiswahili discourse. Although emoji use has increased in social media communication, insufficient attention has been given to how emojis signal the communicator’s stance, reinforce utterances, reduce or increase ambiguity, and perform speech acts in relation to context and the sender’s intention. The study was guided by Sperber and Wilson’s (1995) Relevance Theory and adopted a descriptive design. The main data comprised 285 emojis from 11 categories, purposively collected from Kiswahili discourse on WhatsApp and X. In addition, 50 participants were purposively selected to interpret and validate emoji meanings in context. Supplementary data were collected through questionnaires, interviews, and focus group discussions. The 285 emojis formed the primary data for analysis, while participants’ views supported their interpretation. Data were analysed and presented descriptively. The findings showed that emoji meanings are constructed through the interaction of linguistic, cultural, semiotic, technological, and interactional factors. Emojis were found to signal the communicator’s stance and intention, reinforce or modify the force of utterances, perform speech acts, and guide interpretation according to context. This study contributes to understanding emojis as pragmatic resources and provides a foundation for future research on natural language processing using artificial intelligence and the advancement of African languages in modern technology.

items.title: Narrative Lookahead in LLMs: Event-Level Decodability, Predictive Advantage, and Steering
items.abstract: Do language models carry information about narrative events before writing them, and how far ahead? We examine narrative lookahead through salient, state-changing events rather than tokens or response-level attributes. We extract 23,355 LLM-annotated events from 2,000 stories generated by four open-weight LLMs, labeling them along three nonexclusive dimensions of change: within agents, between agents, and in the story world, with human validation on a subset. Event segmentation and plot-independent labels enable comparisons across stories at horizons measured in events rather than in tokens. items.title: Neuro-Symbolic Artificial Intelligence: Integrating Large Language Models with SMT Solvers, Knowledge Graphs, and Formal Automated Theorem Provers
items.abstract: Abstract—Modern deep neural networks, particularly autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs), have achieved state-of-the-art empirical performance across natural language generation, semantic translation, and broad pattern recognition. However, pure statistical connectionist architectures suffer from fundamental epistemological limitations: ungrounded factual hallucinations, an inability to guarantee mathematical soundness across multi-step deduction, brittle out-of-distribution reasoning, and a complete lack of formal explainability. Conversely, classical symbolic Artificial Intelligence (AI)—encompassing Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT) solvers, formal interactive theorem provers (e.g., Lean 4, Coq, Isabelle), and first-order ontological Knowledge Graphs—provides deterministic logical rigor, provable soundness, and certified safety verification, yet struggles with ambiguous perceptual inputs, continuous representations, and combinatorial state space explosion. Neuro-Symbolic AI establishes a transformative synthesis uniting statistical neural learning with rigorous symbolic reasoning. This paper presents an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical survey and empirical benchmark of neuro-symbolic systems across three mission-critical domains: automated mathematical olympiad proving, certified software verification, and high-stakes autonomous policy execution. We formalize differentiable fuzzy logic t-norm relaxations, model neural-guided proof search over formal tactic trees, and evaluate verified feedback loops using SMT counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR). Furthermore, we construct an empirical evaluation testbed across 1,000 rigorous verification problems spanning the miniF2F formal mathematics benchmark, SMT-LIB program assertions, and complex multi-hop knowledge graphs. Our empirical findings demonstrate that neuro-symbolic integration elevates formal Lean 4 theorem proving success from 28.4% (pure LLM sampling) to 64.2% while guaranteeing 100% mathematical soundness. Concurrently, SMT-guided neural code repair eliminates 94.6% of verified runtime invariant violations. Finally, we formulate open challenges in end-to-end differentiable symbolic unification, scalable bidirectional semantic parsing, and certified neuro-symbolic alignment. Index Terms—Neuro-Symbolic AI, Automated Theorem Proving, Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT), Lean 4, Formal Verification, Knowledge Graphs, Differentiable Logic, Proof Search.

items.title: Neuro-Symbolic Task Allocation for Heterogeneous Warehouse Robots with Versioned Knowledge Updates
items.abstract: Dynamic warehouse task allocation must coordinate loading, transport and unloading robots under changing conditions. We propose a versioned neuro-symbolic architecture in which DeepSeek proposes facts and restricted rules, an authenticated semantic shield validates them, and a mivar-inspired knowledge layer supports deterministic allocation. Stage A selects bounded dispatch candidates using CP-SAT; Stage B performs conflict-aware route and unloading-service search. The service graph supports single-carrier, abstract coalition and same-origin batch transport. Frozen evaluation separates allocation (1800 simulation runs), grounding (6102 responses) and cached-DeepSeek effects (60 episodes). Equal-map-family semantic exactness was 99.52% for facts and 93.02% for rules, but only 69.53% for moving-congestion rules. Cached restricted rules met prespecified simulator-level non-inferiority criteria for deadline misses, distance and a distance-based energy proxy. An additional 150 exploratory episodes evaluate candidate size, early unloading-robot selection, semantic shielding and emulated asynchronous integration. A separately frozen test issued 1248 new API requests on 416 synthetic events. With the contemporaneous backend, revised prompting achieved 320/320 correct congestion transactions versus 317/320 with the original prompt, without significant template-level superiority (Holm-adjusted p = 0.50). Typed-field compilation also reached 320/320 but failed validation on 10/32 access-restriction events. Complete trusted structured inputs do not require an LLM. The contribution is an auditable, bounded semantic interface; physical-robot safety, live-network reliability and physical-energy benefits remain unvalidated.

items.title: New Competencies for the Digital Doctor
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping clinical medicine, requiring physicians to develop competencies that extend beyond traditional biomedical expertise into data literacy, algorithm interpretation, prompt design, and interdisciplinary collaboration with technical teams. As predictive models increasingly influence diagnosis, treatment planning, and healthcare system operations, clinicians must understand how algorithms are trained, validated, and deployed, as well as how to recognize bias, uncertainty, and performance limitations. This chapter outlines a progressive framework of expertise ranging from basic clinical users of AI tools to clinician-scientists and clinician-engineers who co-design and evaluate intelligent health systems. It examines how digital professionalism, ethical stewardship, regulatory awareness, and patient communication must evolve in parallel with technical capability. Ultimately, the digital doctor is not defined by programming proficiency but by the ability to interpret machine-generated insight responsibly and integrate it with human judgment to ensure that artificial intelligence strengthens equitable, safe, and patient-centered care.

items.title: Nine Fallacies of Professional AI Usage: An Evidence-Based Synthesis
items.abstract: Organizations are adopting generative AI and AI decision support in professional work while evidence on their effects is still accumulating. Empirical studies document substantial productivity gains in some settings and losses in others, and practitioners carry assumptions formed during early use into everyday professional work. Research on the resulting problems is spread across human factors, human-computer interaction, fairness research, empirical economics and law, and no consolidated framework for professional use was found. This paper proposes such a framework. Its format is inspired by the Fallacies of Distributed Computing, a short list of false assumptions well known in software engineering; its content is specific to professional AI usage. Through an integrative review of peer-reviewed studies, randomized and preregistered trials, court decisions, provider documentation and regulation, nine fallacies are derived: (1) the output is correct; (2) capability is uniform across tasks; (3) the human reviewer is a reliable safeguard; (4) perceived productivity equals actual productivity; (5) AI removes work; (6) accountability moves to the tool or vendor; (7) skills and system understanding stay intact when work is delegated; (8) results transfer from benchmarks and pilots; and (9) the model is available. For each fallacy, the paper explains why the assumption persists, presents the evidence against it, states the conditions under which it does hold, and grades the strength of the evidence. It then analyzes how fallacies can compound, with particular attention to agent-built software systems that may become difficult to maintain when AI access is lost. The paper closes with implications for practice, a research agenda and a self-assessment instrument.

items.title: Noise-resilient training of machine learning interatomic potentials
items.abstract: The accuracy of machine learning interatomic potentials suffers from reference data that contain numerical noise. Often originating from unconverged or inconsistent electronic-structure calculations, this noise is challenging to identify. Existing mitigation strategies, such as manual filtering or iterative refinement of outliers, require either substantial expert effort or multiple expensive retraining cycles, making them difficult to scale to large datasets. Here, we introduce a noise-resilient training method that automatically down-weighs noisy samples, without requiring additional reference calculations. By tracking the loss distribution via an exponential moving average, this unsupervised method identifies outliers throughout a single training run. We show that this approach prevents overfitting and matches the performance of iterative refinement baselines with significantly reduced overhead. The method’s effectiveness is demonstrated by recovering accurate physical observables for liquid water from unconverged reference data, including diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, we validate its scalability by training a foundation model for organic chemistry on the SPICE dataset, where it reduces both energy and force errors. This framework provides a simple, automated solution for training robust models on imperfect datasets across dataset sizes.

items.title: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH HAZARDS AMONG MEDICAL STUDENTS DURING CLINICAL TRAINING
items.abstract: Medical students occupy an unusual position in the hospital: they are learners, yet they work in the same wards, theatres, and emergency rooms as fully trained staff, often with the least experience, the least authority, and the fewest protective habits. This narrative article reviews the occupational health hazards they face during clinical training and argues that these hazards are neither rare nor incidental, but structural. The hazards are organized into five families — biological (needlestick injuries and blood borne pathogens such as HIV, hepatitis B and C, and tuberculosis), chemical (antineoplastic drugs, anaesthetic gases, disinfectants), physical (radiation, noise, slips and falls), ergonomic (patient handling, long standing hours), and psychological (sleep deprivation, burnout, depression, and bullying) — each illustrated with examples and, where possible, figures from the published literature. Tables summarize the hazard categories and the reasons students are disproportionately exposed. The article concludes that protecting students requires more than personal protective equipment: it demands vaccination, safety-engineered devices, enforced reporting systems, duty hour limits, and above all a clinical culture in which asking for help is a sign of professionalism rather than weakness.

items.title: Occupational Heat Stress and Kidney Health Among Construction Workers: A Review of Emerging Evidence
items.abstract: This paper presents a structured narrative review of ten empirical studies published between 2008 and 2025, examining the relationships between heat exposure, hydration and kidney-related outcomes among construction workers. The studies were identified through targeted searches of Scopus and PubMed and interpreted using an ergonomics-informed work systems perspective. The findings suggest that construction workers are frequently exposed to heat levels that exceed recommended safety thresholds, with dehydration remaining common under real-world site conditions. Across the studies, there are indications of recurring kidney stress, including biomarkers associated with acute kidney injury (AKI), although reported rates vary due to differences in study design and measurement methods. Evidence relating to longer-term outcomes is still limited and remains inconclusive. A key contribution of this study is the development of a conceptual framework that brings together environmental heat exposure, pathophysiological response pathways and organisational and behavioural influences within a work systems context. This framework suggests that heat-related kidney risk is influenced not only by environmental exposure, but also by the interaction between work demands, organisational conditions and the factors that shape worker behaviours. Evidence points towards the need for multi-level strategies to protect workers, including better hydration practices, more adaptive work–rest scheduling and improved occupational health monitoring. The review also highlights important gaps in current knowledge, particularly the need for more longitudinal research and greater consistency in how outcomes are measured. Addressing heat-related kidney risks will be increasingly important for protecting worker health and supporting safe and sustainable construction practices in a warming climate.

items.title: Omni-RS: Unifying Multi-Task Understanding and Generation in Remote Sensing
items.abstract: Practical remote sensing applications often require both understanding and generation capabilities for the same geographic scene. However, most existing methods address either understanding or generation in isolation, while existing unified remote sensing models' generative ability is limited to text-to-image. To bridge this gap, we propose Omni-RS, a unified framework supporting four remote sensing understanding tasks and five generation tasks. Specifically, we introduce the "Scene-Guided Two-Stage Training" strategy, which first adapts a multimodal large language model to remote sensing understanding and then uses its hidden states to guide a diffusion transformer for image generation. To enable joint learning across diverse generation tasks, we construct UniGen, a unified multi-task generation dataset, by organizing heterogeneous remote sensing data into a unified format. Furthermore, we introduce "Detailed Visual Conditioning", which uses visual conditions encoded by a VAE to guide the generation process, thereby supporting additional generation tasks that require reference images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Omni-RS performs exceptionally well in understanding tasks and has achieved outstanding results in a variety of generative tasks.

items.title: On Artificial Intelligence as Assistive Technology in Archaeological Scholarship
items.abstract: In archaeological scholarship, the challenge of interpreting large amounts of fragmented evidence can be daunting. This paper will examine how artificial intelligence can assist in this process, mainly through examining visual evidence and classifying material evidence. Drawing from Trevor Paglen's argument of machine vision and Matteo Pasquinelli's history of classification in machines, this paper develops an analysis of two archaeological case studies: archaeological site detection based on satellite imagery in Mesopotamia and deep-learning classification of Tusayan White Ware pottery. The findings of the studies demonstrate that artificial intelligence is capable of expanding preliminary surveys as well as applying typologies consistently. At the same time, they also highlight the importance of human input, coming to the conclusion that artificial intelligence's potential and principal contribution lies in simplifying the archaeological process and directing human attention towards evidence requiring further interpretation, establishing a framework for understanding artificial intelligence as an assistive technology.

items.title: One-Sided Verification Under Limited Expert Review
items.abstract: AI has become increasingly helpful in scientific discovery, yet human expert review remains essential for those problems without reliable automated evaluation, posing a fundamental challenge as candidate generation scales beyond available review capacity. This paper studies verification under limited human effort, where rare valid solutions need to be prioritized while invalid candidates should be filtered out to reduce human workload. We adopt the one-sided verification objective that maximizes the rejection rate of invalid solutions (TNR) under a constraint on the false-rejection rate of valid ones (FNR), making human review cost an explicit term to minimize. Drawing on the intuition that verifying a specific error can be easier than discovering one, we introduce OSVerify, an algorithmic framework that decouples error proposal from error validation. The error proposer searches for errors in solutions across different granularities by hierarchical decomposition, while the validator distinguishes substantial errors from minor or hallucinated ones. Experiments on competition- and research-level benchmarks show that OSVerify reduces the number of human reviews of invalid solutions by 46% on average compared to voting baselines under the same empirical low FNR constraint. Our post-training of the validator further improves the reduction to 57%. As high-impact real-world use cases, we apply OSVerify to identify errors in published research papers that are subsequently confirmed by the original authors and help resolve three Langlands open conjectures that are confirmed by experts, demonstrating its utility to facilitate human-AI research collaboration.

items.title: Ontologies in Precision Agriculture—A brief Survey on Reproducibility
items.abstract: Combined with machine learning techniques, ontologies have recently been applied widely to enhance decision-making, reasoning, knowledge management and representation, and information retrieval in various domains. Likewise, the popularity of ontologies is increasing in the rapidly evolving field of precision agriculture due to the ability to encode general domain knowledge and specialized knowledge of farmers and utilize it within data processing and analytics pipelines. Although the research on ontologies applied to precision agriculture problems is increasing, adopting published solutions is rather cumbersome, mainly due to low reproducibility of these works. This article is intended to survey the current applied research in ontologies within the agricultural domain, by investigating the used methodologies, technologies and evaluation approaches, the availability of the data, ontologies and source codes developed. It was found that the used data sources, the developed ontologies and the developed source codes are available only in 14%, 9% and 7%, respectively, of the selected 85 articles. Additionally, it was found that the applied methodologies, in relation to the issue of reproducibility, the top-down/bottom-up, semi-automatic, seven-step and ontology matching approaches have shown greater potential, while according to the applied technologies, World Wide Web (W3C) have shown greater contribution compared to artificial intelligence (AI).

items.title: Operator workload responses to a VR-based cognitive and motor task before and after a 30-day simulated ICE mission: A multimodal ergonomic assessment
items.abstract: In isolated, confined and extreme (ICE) environments, prolonged sensory monotony, limited space and sustained task demands may affect operators’ cognitive performance and workload state, with potential consequences for mission safety and system reliability. This small-sample exploratory longitudinal repeated-measures study involved seven male participants in a 30-day simulated ICE mission and examined operator responses to a virtual reality (VR) cognitive and motor task at the pre-isolation and post-isolation measurement windows. The experimental factors were the pre-isolation and post-isolation measurement windows and the pre-VR and post-VR task phases. At each window, participants completed Stroop, Vigilance and reversed digit memory tasks, while cognitive task performance, subjective scales, VR movement behavior, electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) signals were recorded. After Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate (BH-FDR) correction, the clearest changes occurred in the Stroop task. Compared with the pre-isolation measurement window, the post-isolation window showed a higher Stroop completion count, a lower average reaction time and lower EEG Delta-band wavelet amplitude in the left occipital lobe, right occipital lobe, left motor cortex and left prefrontal cortex. In the pre-VR versus post-VR comparison, Stroop completion count increased and average reaction time decreased after VR. Other results from EEG effective connectivity, fNIRS, subjective scales, VR behavior and cross-modal associations did not show similarly stable corrected differences. The findings indicate that cognitive performance and neurophysiological measures describe different aspects of operator-state changes during confined, high-demand operations and may inform operator workload assessment, multimodal state monitoring and VR task design in ICE and similar operational environments.

items.title: Optical and Photonic Computing for Deep Learning Acceleration: Silicon Photonics, Mach-Zehnder Meshes, and Wavelength-Division Multiplexing
items.abstract: Abstract—The relentless exponential scaling of foundation models and transformer architectures has pushed conventional silicon complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) digital accelerators (GPUs, TPUs) toward fundamental thermodynamic and interconnect boundaries. Joule heating, resistance-capacitance (RC) interconnect delay scaling, and the 'memory wall' severely constrain energy efficiency and compute density. Optical Computing and Integrated Silicon Photonics (SiPh) establish an analog non-Von Neumann hardware paradigm that executes fundamental linear algebra operations—specifically General Matrix-Matrix Multiplication (GEMM)—at the speed of light with near-zero runtime energy dissipation. By encoding vector-matrix activations into coherent optical wave fields and modulating light through cascaded Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) meshes, Micro-Ring Resonator (MRR) banks, and Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (WDM) waveguides, photonic tensor processing units (PTPUs) execute analog matrix multiplications in continuous time with sub-nanosecond propagation latencies. However, translating integrated photonic circuits into production deep learning accelerators introduces profound optoelectronic engineering bottlenecks: analog noise accumulation across deep optical meshes, severe thermal phase drift, limited electro-optic Digital-to-Analog / Analog-to-Digital (DAC/ADC) conversion resolution, non-linear activation implementation hurdles, and wafer-scale optical footprint scaling. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of integrated photonic computing for deep neural network acceleration. We formalize the Clements and Reck unitary matrix decomposition algorithms over reconfigurable MZI topologies, derive the optical transmission transfer matrix under optical carrier phase error perturbations, and establish energy-per-MAC physical thermodynamic bounds across electro-optic conversion interfaces. Furthermore, we construct an empirical co-simulation and hardware testbed benchmarking silicon photonic meshes against state-of-the-art CMOS accelerators (NVIDIA H100, Google TPU v5p) across vision transformers, large language model attention heads, and resonant graph convolutions. Our empirical findings demonstrate that a 64x64 integrated MZI photonic mesh achieves a 58.4x improvement in energy-delay product (EDP) over 4nm digital CMOS cores, sustaining up to 128 Tera-Operations per Second per Watt (TOPS/W) at 4-bit to 8-bit equivalent precision, while active thermo-optic phase stabilization preserves 98.2% baseline classification accuracy. Finally, we establish open research directions in all-optical non-linear activation functions, co-packaged optical memory architectures, and wafer-scale photonic interconnect scaling. Index Terms—Photonic Computing, Silicon Photonics (SiPh), Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI), Wavelength-Division Multiplexing (WDM), Optical Neural Networks (ONNs), Matrix-Vector Multiplication, Energy-Efficient Accelerators.

items.title: PAINT: A Framework for Multilingual Pain Representation from Medical Licensing Exams to Real-World Clinical Texts
items.abstract: Pain is one of the most common and clinically important symptoms, reflecting disease onset, progression, and treatment response. However, pain is difficult to accurately capture and interpret from medical text, as its expression varies across languages, documentation types, and patient demographics, and is often embedded in terminology, negation, temporality, and contextual descriptions. Existing pain-related studies remain largely monolingual or limited to narrow clinical settings. In this study, we introduce PAINT, a multilingual framework for studying pain representation across medical exams and real-world clinical texts. PAINT includes nine pain-focused dataset partitions spanning English, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese, with clinician annotations in all four languages. We curated a structured schema covering pain relevance, pain presence, anatomical location, pain descriptors, and demographic information. To capture multilingual pain representations, we leverage large language models (LLMs) and adopt an ensemble strategy to improve performance. Ten clinicians across four languages validate the labels: the ensemble reaches macro-F1 of 0.91-1.00 on pain relevance and pain presence and 92-100% accuracy on demographics, with inter-annotator $κ$ of 0.82-1.00. We release the WorldMedQA-Pain ensemble labels, the extraction pipeline, validation scripts, and clinician annotation sheets for publicly licensed corpora, providing a foundation for pain-centered clinical NLP and for studying pain documentation across languages and healthcare contexts.

items.title: Pareto optimization of textual and engagement features for crime-related social media analytics
items.abstract: Crime-related social media content provides valuable information for situational awareness and policy support; however, engagement-driven signals, such as likes and retweets, can introduce popularity bias and affect predictive outcomes. This study proposes a fairness-aware, Pareto-based, multi-objective optimization framework for feature selection and Random Forest hyperparameter optimization, leveraging textual and engagement features. A dataset of 32,000 crime-related tweets covering Fraud, Accident, and Murder was represented using TF-IDF and interaction-based features. Four optimization strategies, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning (ERL), and Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), were comparatively evaluated. NSGA-II jointly maximized classification performance while minimizing a fairness penalty based on Statistical Parity Difference (SPD), Disparate Impact (DI), and Equality of Opportunity Difference (EOD). In this study, fairness refers to mitigating engagement-driven popularity bias across behavioral user groups rather than demographic discrimination. NSGA-II achieved an accuracy of 0.8118 and an F1-score of 0.8051, with an SPD of 0.08, DI of 0.97, and EOD of 0.06, demonstrating the most favorable balance between predictive performance and behavioral fairness. Although removing engagement features improved standalone Accuracy and F1-score, retaining them enabled explicit assessment and mitigation of engagement-driven bias. Stratified cross-validation and comparative analysis across the optimization strategies further supported the consistency of the observed results. The findings demonstrate that integrating fairness objectives directly into Pareto-based optimization provides a practical and interpretable approach to balancing predictive effectiveness and engagement-driven fairness in crime-related social media analytics.

items.title: PEAS-DeiT: Multi-Scale Spatial Attention Enhanced DeiT for Pea Leaf Disease Classification
items.abstract: Early and accurate detection of pea diseases is essential for reducing crop losses and supporting precision agriculture. Although deep learning methods have shown good performance in plant disease classification, CNN-based models may have limitations in learning long-range relationships and detailed disease features. In this study, an explainable transformer-based framework, named PEAS-DeiT, is proposed for automated pea leaf disease classification. The proposed approach integrates a multi-scale spatial attention mechanism into the Data-efficient Image Transformer (DeiT) architecture to enhance the representation of disease-related visual features. A unified pea leaf disease dataset (UPLDD) was constructed by combining multiple publicly available datasets, covering six classes, including five disease categories and healthy samples. The proposed model was evaluated against CNN-based and transformer-based architectures using five-fold cross-validation. Furthermore, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) analysis was performed to investigate the regions contributing to model predictions. Experimental results demonstrate that PEAS-DeiT achieved an accuracy of 93.11%, showing competitive performance compared with the evaluated CNN and transformer-based models. The gradient-based saliency analysis also revealed localized response patterns in several evaluated samples, providing qualitative insight into the image regions contributing to model predictions. Statistical analyses were conducted to evaluate the performance differences among the compared models. These findings indicate that PEAS-DeiT provides a competitive approach for pea leaf disease classification within the evaluated experimental setting.

items.title: Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction through LoRA Federated Training
items.abstract: In Intelligent Transport Systems, protecting vulnerable road users, specifically pedestrians, is a paramount challenge. The present work contributes to this field, putting forth a distributed architecture in which vehicles connected to the cellular infrastructure collect pedestrians' trajectories and fine-tune a foundation model for pedestrian trajectory forecasting via federated training. A server positioned at the edge of the cellular network is responsible for aggregating the local model's parameters from the vehicles and updating the global model's parameters. To reduce radio resource utilization, Low-Rank Adaptation is proposed; to decrease both the number and the size of updates, an increase in the number of training rounds performed by the vehicles per communication round is put forth. A novel figure of merit is then introduced to quantify the use of radio resources dedicated to Vehicle-to-Infrastructure communications as required by the federated solution. The proposed scheme delivers excellent prediction accuracy while significantly reducing the communication cost compared to alternative federated training methods. This shows that combining fine-tuning, Low-Rank Adaptation, and a reduction of the communication periodicity between the vehicles and the edge server is key to enabling a distributed approach to trajectory prediction in vehicular environments.

items.title: Pemanfaatan Generative Artificial Intelligence untuk Peningkatan Kapasitas Digital Marketing bagi UMKM Makanan dan Minuman di Kecamatan Bojongloa Kaler, Kota Bandung
items.abstract: Micro, small, and medium enterprises require practical digital marketing skills to produce attractive and consistent promotional content. This program aimed to strengthen the digital marketing capacity of 30 food and beverage MSMEs in Bojongloa Kaler District, Bandung City, through Generative Artificial Intelligence-based training and mentoring. Activities were implemented through needs identification, material and instrument preparation, interactive training, guided practice, mentoring, evaluation, and follow-up support. The training covered an introduction to GenAI, prompt engineering, caption writing, product descriptions, content ideas, promotional calendars, and simple digital design. Evaluation results showed that participants' average understanding increased from 54.2% in the pre-test to 96.4% in the post-test, representing a 42.2 percentage-point improvement. Participants produced reusable outputs, including captions, product descriptions, prompt templates, content calendars, and digital promotional materials. Although long-term sales and social media performance were not measured, these outputs provide a foundation for future monitoring and independent content production.

items.abstract: The rapid growth of the digital economy has opened vast opportunities through gig economy platforms, yet high school students and teachers often lack the digital literacy and skills needed to capitalize on these prospects productively. This community service program aimed to empower the economic potential of students and teachers at SMA IRA Medan by delivering education and technical training on digital freelance platforms integrated with Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Deep Learning tools. The methodology comprised three main stages: pre-implementation (need analysis, module synthesis, and institutional coordination), implementation (interactive seminar, live demonstration of AI tools, and hands-on portfolio creation workshops), and evaluation (pre-test/post-test analysis and mentoring). The activity took place at SMA IRA Medan on September 30, 2026, involving 40 participants consisting of students and teachers. The results demonstrated a significant increase in participant understanding, rising from an average of 23.1% in the pre-test to 88.8% in the post-test, an increase of 65.7%. Furthermore, 87.5% of participants successfully created active profiles and digital portfolios on platforms such as Sribulancer and Projects.co.id. This initiative successfully fostered a digital entrepreneurship mindset, equipping students and teachers with monetizable skills to support sustainable economic independence.

items.title: People as Sensors: An End-to-End Deep Learning Framework for Near-Real-Time Wildfire Detection, Classification, and Geospatial Intelligence from Greek Social Media
items.abstract: Citizens' social media posts can provide rapid, complementary situational information during emerging wildfires, alongside conventional sensing and official reporting. For Greek, no annotated wildfire corpus or end-to-end pipeline existed, and most systems stop at binary detection or depend on geotags. We present an end-to-end Greek-language NLP pipeline, a research prototype that turns keyword-retrieved, unlabeled X posts into a geolocated, near-real-time wildfire map: it detects active fires, types them as wildland, urban, or mixed, resolves toponyms, and clusters reports into incidents. On 3,277 manually annotated posts from two fire seasons, to our knowledge the first publicly released, agreement-audited Greek wildfire corpus, fine-tuned transformers reached F2 = 0.911 for detection and macro-F1 = 0.874 for fire type, outperforming classical baselines and, under the tested prompting conditions, two large language models, faster and at zero API cost. On a chronological hold-out of the unseen 2025 season, detection retains F2 = 0.850 (classification recall 0.907); fire-type classification degrades more (macro-F1 0.769 ± 0.085). Spatiotemporal toponym disambiguation raised geocoding accuracy from 54.68% to 80.58% (p < 0.001); a repeatability test revealed gazetteer drift. In a retrospective replay of 12 August 2024 posts, it resolved hundreds of reports of an Attica wildfire into one incident cluster, complementing emergency calls.

items.title: Perception of AI-induced occupational replacement risk and withdrawal behavior: an identity threat perspective in the workplace
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into the workplace, the risk that occupations will be replaced by AI has received widespread attention. Nevertheless, the underlying mechanisms linking AI-induced occupational replacement risk perception to individual withdrawal behaviors remain underexplored. Taking identity threat as an explanatory lens, this study integrates Identity Threat Theory (ITT) and Technology Threat Avoidance Theory (TTAT) to investigate the effect of occupational replacement risk perception on employee withdrawal behavior, with professional identity, work meaningfulness, and job insecurity serving as mediators and technological self-efficacy as a moderator. Two studies were conducted to test the theoretical model developed in this research. Study 1 developed and validated the AI-induced occupational replacement risk perception scale. Study 2 employed a three-wave time-lagged survey design to test the hypotheses. The results show that occupational replacement risk perception is positively associated with withdrawal behavior through decreased professional identity and work meaningfulness as well as increased job insecurity. Furthermore, these indirect effects are weaker among employees with higher technological self-efficacy. By illuminating the identity-threat mechanism that links AI-induced occupational replacement risk perception to employee behavior, this study opens the black box of how AI shapes employee responses, and it concludes with a discussion of the theoretical contributions and practical implications of these findings.

items.title: Performance evaluation and interpretability of a Qwen LangGraph agent for AI written and AI rewritten text detection
items.abstract: Abstract The widespread adoption of large language models has increased the need to distinguish human-authored text from AI-generated content, including cases in which generated text is subsequently rewritten or paraphrased. In practice, many detectors output only a single AI-likelihood score or percentage, offering limited transparency and little indication of whether a passage appears directly AI-written (AIW) or AI-rewritten (AIR). This study presents an agentic detection framework for two connected tasks: binary provenance detection (Human versus AI) and conditional subtype detection (AIW versus AIR). The dataset combined the Human-ChatGPT Comparison Corpus (HC3) and the ai-text-detection-pile with 4,348 pre-generated AIR records produced by a single GPT-based rewriting workflow. The proposed Qwen–LangGraph AI agent was compared to a HashingVectorizer–TF-IDF–SGD classifier, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall, and ELECTRA-small. On the binary test set, DeBERTa-v3-xsmall achieved the best discrimination (99.4995% accuracy and 99.9911% AUROC), whereas the agent achieved 98.8816% accuracy and 99.9187% AUROC. On the AI-only test set (10,769 AIW; 1,274 AIR), the agent obtained the highest threshold-based accuracy (96.7367%), macro-F1 (90.0357%), and AIR F1 (81.8643%), but its AUROC (83.2507%) and AUPR (79.7336%) were lower than those of the DeBERTa-v3-xsmall and ELECTRA-small transformers. Paired DeLong and McNemar analyses with Holm correction showed that the agent improved threshold-based AIR performance over the lexical baseline. Interpretability was operationalised through lexical weights, linguistic and out-of-distribution diagnostics, sentence-level indicators, and route traces. The findings support the use of AI as decision support, not as automated proof of plagiarism or misconduct.

items.title: Personal and Academic Factors in Teachers’ Perceptions of Educational Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: (1) Background: The aim of this study was to analyze how teacher trainees and teachers relate to Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education across socio-emotional, attitudinal, competency-based, and ethical dimensions, considering the influence of personal, academic, and professional variables. The study was conceptually framed by the UNESCO AI Competency Framework for Teachers (AI CFT), complemented by DigCompEdu as a broader reference for teacher digital competence. (2) Methods: A quantitative, non-experimental, descriptive, cross-sectional design was developed with a sample of 1292 participants from Andalusia, consisting mainly of university students, along with teachers. The ACISE-IA scale, consisting of 39 items developed by Serrano-García et al. (2026), was used for data collection. (3) Results: The results showed that age and teaching experience are negatively associated with favorable attitudes and digital competence, while academic performance is positively related to greater openness, critical reflection, and perception of competence. Likewise, significant differences were identified according to the branch of knowledge, employment status, and academic year, with more positive assessments among students and in social science areas. (4) Conclusions: Overall, the findings show that the relationship with AI is not homogeneous, but rather modulated by educational and professional trajectories, underscoring the need to design flexible teacher training models that integrate technological development with pedagogical, emotional, and ethical reflection. These findings also contribute to educational sustainability by highlighting the importance of developing teacher training strategies that support the responsible and sustained integration of AI into educational systems.
